title: Diffuse supernova, Galactic supernova, solar-flare and other astrophysical neutrinos at 248 keV: could a neutrino burst on 16 June 2023 explain the event?
question: Beyond the steady atmospheric flux (P019), which astrophysical neutrino sources (DSNB, Galactic core-collapse SN, SN 2023ixf, solar flares, IceCube diffuse flux, reactor/geo/solar) could give a lone 200-270 keV xenon recoil coherently or via P019's incoherent Fermi-recoil channel, and what fluence would a hypothetical transient at 21:22:39 UTC on 16 June 2023 need?
headline_result: No astrophysical neutrino source beyond the atmospheric flux can give the lone 248 keV recoil: coherent CEvNS needs E_nu >= 123 MeV (E_R,max = 59 keV at 60 MeV) so DSNB/SN spectra are kinematically blind; the incoherent Fermi-recoil channel opens at 30.6 MeV and gives <= 4e-6 (DSNB) and 2-6e-3 per Galactic 10 kpc burst (none occurred); IceCube flux 1.4e-6 GeV-PeV interactions; a burst explanation needs 6e11-3e12 nu cm^-2 above 123 MeV = 3e54 erg at 10 kpc, ~1e6 Super-K events and 450-2400 low-energy LZ companions
key_numbers: E_R,max(15/30/50/60 MeV) = 3.7/14.7/40.8/58.8 keV; E_nu,min(200/248/271 keV) = 110.7/123.3/128.9 MeV; lone-NR threshold 30.6 (225 keV)/32.7 (248)/35.6 MeV (279); gated atmospheric 1.77e-4 vs P019 1.73e-4; DSNB coherent 4e-15-3e-9, lone-NR 1.8e-7-4.1e-6; SN 10 kpc 27 CEvNS/t, 23-46 ROI recoils, coherent window 1.9e-8-4.2e-6, lone-NR 2.0-5.9e-3 per burst; SN 1 kpc lone-NR 0.2, 0.2 kpc 5; SN 2023ixf 5e-14/5e-9; IceCube 1.4e-6 interactions (sigma 4e-34 cm^2 at 100 TeV), 1e-18 with E_had < 300 keV; F_req = 1.18e12 (150 MeV), 5.7e11 (300 MeV), 9.0e11 cm^-2 (E^-2.5 tail); E_iso 3.4e54 erg at 10 kpc, 3.4e52 at 1 kpc; Super-K 6e5-1.2e6 IBD events; N_lo 893 (150 MeV)/451 (300 MeV); solar flare <= 8e-6 (SK-limit 1e7 cm^-2 at 150 MeV); magnetar giant flare 4e-9
model_or_mechanism: CEvNS with Helm form factor (P019 conventions) on Keil-Raffelt pinched spectra (alpha = 2.5) for DSNB/SN; Llewellyn-Smith NC quasi-elastic knock-out with Pauli blocking + residual-nucleus Fermi recoil (P019 channel) with a new impulse-approximation energy threshold p_max = E + sqrt(2 m_n (E - S_n - E_R)); DIS interaction count for the IceCube flux; required-fluence inversion with energy budget, Super-K IBD response and LZ low-energy companion count
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - excludes all non-atmospheric astrophysical neutrino origins, steady or transient
result_type: computed (kinematics, thresholds, CEvNS counts, required fluence) / estimated (incoherent factors, recalled normalisations)
confidence: high - every channel >= 1e5 below one event under any recalled normalisation; transient exclusion has two data-independent legs (Super-K, LZ companions)
